blocks.text: Condo buildings in Queens Park
(3) Two name traps are excluded in: Queen's Park Estate is in Queensborough, and Queens Terrace / Amara Terrace are in Uptown NW — neither belongs to this sub-area despite the names.
Moody on the Hill — 232 Sixth Street

A 6-storey mid-rise at the corner of 6th and Welsh Street, built in 2024; current listings record property type Apartment/Condo, year built 2024, a rooftop patio among the building features, and unit-level pets as cats OK / pets with restrictions, with parking and storage.
Streets, schools and getting around Queens Park

items.t: Queens Park is a central mainland neighbourhood in the City of New Westminster between Royal Avenue and Sixth Avenue, and between Sixth Street and McBride Boulevard, with Queen's Park itself in the eastern portion of the neighbourhood. Glenbrooke North is to the north, Downtown and the Quay to the south, Uptown to the west along Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue, and Sapperton beyond McBride Boulevard to the east.

New Westminster community-level context (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, not for Queens Park): Condos & Townhomes median sale price $560,000, $587/sqft, sale-to-list 95%, 27 days on market in September 2026.

Transit anchors: no SkyTrain station is inside Queens Park; the nearest stations are Columbia Station and New Westminster Station (Expo Line); TransLink route 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and route 102 (Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station) serve the adjoining corridors. Moody on the Hill's marketing puts Columbia and New Westminster stations at a 10-minute walk from its Sixth Street corner.

Main roads: Royal Avenue, Sixth Avenue, Sixth Street and McBride Boulevard bound and cross the area; McBride Boulevard links north to East Columbia Street and Sapperton and south toward the Pattullo Bridge approach. Queen's Park offers a rose garden, spray park, picnic shelters, tennis and pickleball courts, sports fields and stadium, a skate park, an off-leash dog park, Queen's Park Arena and the Queen's Park Sportsplex.

items.t: Heritage Conservation Area — the defining overlay for this sub-area: the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area is currently the only HCA in New Westminster; it places a layer of heritage protection over ALL properties in the area regardless of construction age, classed Protected or Non-protected. Building Permit applications for work such as new buildings, demolition, or changes affecting the front, sides or visible roofline of Protected properties, and subdivision applications, require a Heritage Alteration Permit (HAP) reviewed for design-guideline compliance, and Protected properties also need an HAP for exterior changes that do not require a Building Permit. Protected properties are also under the Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw; standard in-kind maintenance does not require an HAP; Protected-property incentives include additional density, special BC Building Code provisions, density transfer, relaxed laneway/carriage house guidelines and no heritage permit fees. How the HCA applies to a strata building's common-property exterior work is a per-property City question — confirm for the specific building before pricing exterior work.
Flood / hazards: the governing overlay here is heritage, not floodplain — a floodplain zone for this area is UNVERIFIED in the sources read.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queens Park

items.t: The apostrophe is a filing system. "Queens Park" (board, no apostrophe) vs "Queen's Park" (City, with apostrophe) is not pedantry — documents, permits and the HCA itself are filed under the City spelling, listings under the board spelling, and searching only one misses the other half of the record.

Three "Queens" buildings belong to other sub-areas. Queen's Park Estate is a Queensborough townhouse project (240 Jardine Street), and Queens Terrace and Amara Terrace are Uptown NW buildings on Queens Avenue — a buyer searching "Queens" names assembles a stock list for three different sub-areas and none of them is this one.

The rezoning for the area's one new building is on the public record. Council adopted Zoning Amendment (228–232 Sixth Street) Bylaw No. 7996, 2018 for the old La Rustica restaurant site — the approval history behind Moody on the Hill, inside a heritage conservation area where a new mid-rise is the exception that proves the HCA rule.

Protected status can add value, not just process. Protected-property incentives in the HCA include additional density, density transfer, relaxed laneway/carriage house guidelines and no heritage permit fees — the same classification that triggers Heritage Alteration Permits also carries development value a Non-protected property does not.
A zero-sale month says nothing about values here.

The park is inside the neighbourhood, not beside it. Queen's Park sits in the eastern portion of the neighbourhood itself, with the Arena and Sportsplex in it — "steps to Queen's Park" listing copy for the residential streets around it describes the sub-area's own centre, not an amenity in the next area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Queens Park

items.t: THE defining diligence item for this sub-area is the Heritage Conservation Area — not floodplain: (a floodplain zone for Queens Park is UNVERIFIED; Zone 3 belongs to the Quay and Downtown NW files and is never imported here). The Queen's Park HCA is currently the only HCA in New Westminster: all properties in it are classed Protected or Non-protected regardless of age. A Heritage Alteration Permit (HAP) is required for new buildings, demolition, subdivision, and changes to the front, sides or visible roofline of a Protected property — and for some Protected-property exterior changes that need no Building Permit at all. The Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw applies to Protected properties. In-kind maintenance needs no HAP. Protected-property incentives: additional density, density transfer, special Building Code provisions, relaxed laneway/carriage guidelines, and no heritage permit fees. For the counted strata (Clinton Place, built 1974, inside the HCA geography): exterior and common-property work can engage the HAP regime — confirm the parcel's Protected/Non-protected status and the strata's obligations with the City before pricing any exterior project; parcel-level status for any specific property: UNVERIFIED here.

Form B diligence (Clinton Place): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Suites as the City states them: one secondary suite per house; the City allows a property to have both a secondary suite and a laneway/carriage house (Zoning Bylaw s. 190.29 — confirm the current section text in the consolidated bylaw before relying on it); inside the HCA, Protected properties get relaxed laneway/carriage guidelines as an incentive. Adaptable housing: at least 40% of single-storey units in multiple-unit buildings must be adaptable (Adaptable Housing Bylaw 7464, 2011).

Property tax: City of New Westminster taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty applied July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty September 3, 2026. The City also runs its own electrical utility. There is NO Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in New Westminster — that 3% tax is Vancouver only and never applies here.
Presales (REDMA), if any are ever marketed here: disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18), 7-day rescission (REDMA s. 21), deposits in trust. No presale is verified in Queens Park.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queens Park

items.t: The apostrophe is a filing system: board data says "Queens Park," the City says "Queen's Park" — searches, titles and page copy that mix the two will miss records in one spelling or the other.

Protected status ignores age: in the Queen's Park HCA, a 1974 strata and a 1910 house are both classed — Protected or Non-protected — by designation, not by vintage; "it's not a heritage house" is not an exemption argument.

The HCA pays its protected owners back: additional density, density transfer, special Building Code provisions, relaxed laneway/carriage guidelines and zero heritage permit fees are the City's stated incentives for Protected properties — the other half of the permit burden, and routinely left out of listing copy.

The care centre is at the edge, not in the stock: Queen's Park Care Centre (315 McBride Boulevard, 148 publicly subsidized long-term care beds) anchors the McBride edge — it appears in seniors-housing searches for this name and is not purchasable housing of any tenure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Queens Park

items.t: Heritage Conservation Area — the defining rule for lots here: the Queen's Park HCA (Schedule B of the OCP, adopted by OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 7926, 2017) classes every property Protected or Non-protected regardless of age. Building Permit applications for work such as new buildings, demolition, or changes affecting the front, sides or visible roofline of Protected properties, and subdivision applications, require a Heritage Alteration Permit (HAP) reviewed for design-guideline compliance; Protected properties also need an HAP for exterior changes that do not require a Building Permit. Protected properties are also under the City's Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw; standard in-kind maintenance does not require an HAP. Protected-property incentives include additional density, special BC Building Code provisions, density transfer, relaxed laneway/carriage house guidelines and no heritage permit fees.

Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: houses sit under the RS series (s.310) — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5 — overlaid by the HCA. Standing citywide position: New Westminster's townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C plus RT-3/3A/3B only; RT-A/RT-B do not exist, and 836.10 m² is an RM apartment-district density threshold, not an RT figure.
OCP — Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017: the Official Community Plan governing the area, including the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area (Schedule B).

Subdivision + servicing — Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (VERIFIED), plus the HAP layer: the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 requires Approving Officer approval and ensures new lots are adequately serviced and meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements, through the City's pre-application / application / Works & Services Agreement process — and in Queens Park a subdivision application additionally requires a Heritage Alteration Permit. Neither process alone settles a Queens Park split.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Queens Park ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

New Westminster property taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queens Park

items.t: Every lot is classified, old or new: the HCA classes every property Protected or Non-protected regardless of construction age — a brand-new Queens Park house carries the HCA layer exactly as an 1890s house does, and Protected homes need an HAP even for some exterior changes that need no Building Permit.

Deferred maintenance is a bylaw issue here: the Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw sets minimum standards for Protected properties so heritage properties are not lost through neglect — deferred exterior maintenance on a Protected home is both a compliance issue and a negotiation point.
CMHC's published range is 0.6%–4.5%.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Is the Queens Park neighbourhood the same as Queen's Park the park?
faq.a: No. "Queens Park" (no apostrophe) is the MLS® sub-area / neighbourhood name; "Queen's Park" is the City's spelling for the park in the neighbourhood's eastern portion and for the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area covering the residential streets around it.

faq.q: What sold in Queens Park in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing — detached: 0 solds from 7 listings; condos & townhomes: 0 solds from 1 listing, so no sales ratio applies (small-sample warning: one month with zero sales says nothing about values). At the New Westminster community level the detached median sale price was $1,365,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $560,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What does the Heritage Conservation Area mean for a homeowner?
faq.a: Every property in the area is classed Protected or Non-protected regardless of age; new buildings, demolition, subdivision and specified exterior changes need a Heritage Alteration Permit reviewed against the design guidelines, and Protected properties are also under the Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw.

School District 40, address-based. For the sample address 800 Queens Avenue the locator result is École Qayqayt Elementary (K–5), Fraser River Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12); check the exact address in the SD40 locator.

faq.q: Are there really condos in Queens Park, or only houses?
faq.a: Almost only houses. The one verified apartment building is Moody on the Hill (232 Sixth Street, built 2024) at the Sixth Street edge — and even its sub-area label is disputed (see the next question).

faq.q: Is "Queen's Park Estate" a Queens Park condo I can buy into?
faq.a: No — it is a townhouse development at 240 Jardine Street in Queensborough, on the island across the Fraser River. The name is the trap; City records place the Jardine Street townhouse project in Queensborough.

faq.q: What about Queens Terrace and Amara Terrace on Queens Avenue?
faq.a: Queens Avenue the street is not the same geography as Queens Park the sub-area.

faq.q: What does the Heritage Conservation Area mean for a condo purchase here?
faq.a: Every property in the area is classed Protected or Non-protected regardless of age; specified exterior work, new buildings, demolition and subdivision need a Heritage Alteration Permit, and Protected properties carry minimum maintenance standards plus incentives (additional density, density transfer, relaxed laneway/carriage guidelines, no permit fees). For a strata unit the practical exposure is common-property exterior work decided by the strata — ask for the building's Protected/Non-protected status and any HAP history in the strata documents.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Queens Park condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw; the registered bylaws on the Form B govern that question.

faq.q: What townhouses exist in Queens Park?
faq.a: One verified complex: Clinton Place, 114 Park Row — a 14-unit strata townhouse complex (strata plan NWS262) built 1974 among Park Row's heritage houses.

faq.q: "Queen's Park Estate" townhouses — are they in Queens Park?
faq.a: No. Queen's Park Estate is at 240 Jardine Street in Queensborough. The name is the trap; the sub-area, the zoning (RT-3) and the river arm are all different.

faq.q: What does the Heritage Conservation Area actually restrict?
faq.a: For a Protected property: new buildings, demolition, subdivision and any change to the front, sides or visible roofline need a Heritage Alteration Permit — some exterior changes need one even without a Building Permit. Non-protected properties face fewer controls, and in-kind maintenance needs no permit either way. Status is parcel-by-parcel: UNVERIFIED for any address until the City's HCA materials are checked against it.
